deck.title: Effect of Temperature on Reaction Rates & the Concept of Activation Energy

back_blocks.md: An **activation energy** (*E*<sub>a</sub>) is the minimum energy that reactant particles must possess for a collision to be effective and a chemical reaction to occur.

cards.back_md: An **activation energy** (*E*<sub>a</sub>) is the minimum energy that reactant particles must possess for a collision to be effective and a chemical reaction to occur.

front_blocks.md: Why is the activation energy relatively larger for endothermic reactions than for exothermic reactions?

back_blocks.md: In **endothermic** reactions, the products are at a higher energy level than the reactants. The activation energy (*E*<sub>a</sub>) is the energy needed to reach the transition state above the reactants, so *E*<sub>a</sub> tends to be **larger** for endothermic reactions than for **exothermic** ones, where the products lie at lower energy than the reactants.

cards.front_md: Why is the activation energy relatively larger for endothermic reactions than for exothermic reactions?
cards.back_md: In **endothermic** reactions, the products are at a higher energy level than the reactants. The activation energy (*E*<sub>a</sub>) is the energy needed to reach the transition state above the reactants, so *E*<sub>a</sub> tends to be **larger** for endothermic reactions than for **exothermic** ones, where the products lie at lower energy than the reactants.

back_blocks.md: A **Boltzmann distribution curve** is a graph showing the distribution of energies among molecules in a sample at a given temperature. The area under the curve to the right of *E*<sub>a</sub> represents molecules with enough energy to react.

cards.back_md: A **Boltzmann distribution curve** is a graph showing the distribution of energies among molecules in a sample at a given temperature. The area under the curve to the right of *E*<sub>a</sub> represents molecules with enough energy to react.

front_blocks.md: At a given temperature, most molecules in a sample have energies close to or greater than the activation energy.

back_blocks.md: Only a **small proportion** of molecules have energies equal to or greater than *E*<sub>a</sub>. Most molecules have intermediate energies and the curve peaks well below *E*<sub>a</sub> for most reactions.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

At a given temperature, most molecules in a sample have energies close to or greater than the activation energy.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Only a **small proportion** of molecules have energies equal to or greater than *E*<sub>a</sub>. Most molecules have intermediate energies and the curve peaks well below *E*<sub>a</sub> for most reactions.

front_blocks.md: When temperature increases, the Boltzmann distribution curve **..........**  and its peak shifts to the **..........**  , indicating a greater proportion of molecules with energy above *E*<sub>a</sub>.

back_blocks.md: When temperature increases, the Boltzmann distribution curve **flattens** and its peak shifts to the **right**, indicating a greater proportion of molecules with energy above *E*<sub>a</sub>.

cards.front_md: When temperature increases, the Boltzmann distribution curve **..........**  and its peak shifts to the **..........**  , indicating a greater proportion of molecules with energy above *E*<sub>a</sub>.
cards.back_md: When temperature increases, the Boltzmann distribution curve **flattens** and its peak shifts to the **right**, indicating a greater proportion of molecules with energy above *E*<sub>a</sub>.

front_blocks.md: Give two reasons why increasing temperature increases the rate of a chemical reaction.

back_blocks.md:
1. Particles move faster, so **collision frequency** increases, giving more effective collisions per unit time.
2. A **greater proportion** of molecules have kinetic energy exceeding *E*<sub>a</sub>, so a higher fraction of collisions are successful.

cards.front_md: Give two reasons why increasing temperature increases the rate of a chemical reaction.
cards.back_md:
1. Particles move faster, so **collision frequency** increases, giving more effective collisions per unit time.
2. A **greater proportion** of molecules have kinetic energy exceeding *E*<sub>a</sub>, so a higher fraction of collisions are successful.

front_blocks.md: The increase in collision frequency is the main reason why rate increases with temperature.

back_blocks.md: The **greater proportion** of molecules exceeding *E*<sub>a</sub> has a larger effect on rate than the increase in collision frequency alone.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

The increase in collision frequency is the main reason why rate increases with temperature.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

The **greater proportion** of molecules exceeding *E*<sub>a</sub> has a larger effect on rate than the increase in collision frequency alone.

front_blocks.md: On a Boltzmann distribution curve, how is the effect of increasing temperature shown, and what does this indicate about the rate of reaction?

back_blocks.md: The curve **flattens** and the peak moves to **higher energy**. The area under the curve to the right of *E*<sub>a</sub> **increases**, showing more molecules have sufficient energy to react and the rate of reaction increases.

front_blocks.md: For a collision to be effective, particles must collide in the correct **..........**  and possess energy equal to or greater than the **..........** .

back_blocks.md: For a collision to be effective, particles must collide in the correct **orientation** and possess energy equal to or greater than the **activation energy**.
